When the app fits a mathematical curve, it needs starting values for the model parameters. Poor starting values can lead to an unstable or unreasonable fit, especially for nonlinear models. Grid-search initialization reduces this risk by trying many candidate starting-value sets before nonlinear least-squares fitting.

The app evaluates those candidate starts, chooses the most promising one, and then runs the final curve-fitting step from that starting point. This improves robustness, but it does not guarantee that the fit is the global best solution.
